decisions.reason: As the umbrella supplement range, it keeps several low-cost pharmacy-market options open, so a large firm would usually retain it unless the whole line clearly failed.
A skin-and-hair supplement is a crowded, less core category for a pharmaceutical manufacturer, and after several years the option value is likely too low to justify continued attention.
Joint-health supplements fit pharmacy demand and the move from a mention to a dedicated page suggests enough traction to keep the option open a bit longer.
Its differentiated immune positioning and low carrying cost make it a relatively attractive option to retain unless internal sales data are clearly poor.
Despite the 2018 valsartan issue, a generic blood-pressure medicine is close to the firm's core business and more likely to be fixed and continued than abandoned.
An OTC triptan is a strategically relevant adjacent product for a large pharma firm, so it is worth keeping unless post-launch demand has clearly disappointed.
